title: Azure Management Hierarchy
summary: Tenant → management groups → subscriptions → resource groups → resources, and how governance flows down the tree.

nodes.label: Microsoft Entra tenant
nodes.detail: Every subscription trusts exactly one Entra tenant. The tenant holds users, groups and service principals used to sign in and be authorized.

nodes.label: Tenant root group
nodes.detail: Created automatically. Policies or roles assigned here apply to every management group and subscription in the tenant.

nodes.label: Production MG
nodes.detail: Management groups group subscriptions so you can assign Azure Policy and RBAC once. Up to six levels deep below the root.

nodes.label: Non-production MG
nodes.detail: A separate branch lets you apply looser policies to dev/test while production stays strict.

nodes.label: Subscription A
nodes.detail: Subscriptions are billing and limit boundaries. Each has exactly one parent management group.

nodes.label: Subscription B
nodes.detail: Inherits everything assigned at Production MG and the tenant root group.

nodes.label: Subscription C
nodes.detail: Inherits Non-production MG assignments only (plus anything at the root).

nodes.label: RG: web-prod
nodes.detail: A logical container for resources that share a lifecycle. Deleting the RG deletes everything in it.

nodes.label: RG: data-prod
nodes.detail: Resource groups can't be nested, and the RG's location doesn't restrict where its resources are deployed.

nodes.label: RG: sandbox
nodes.detail: Developers might be Contributors here without having any rights in production.

nodes.label: VM
nodes.detail: Resources belong to exactly one resource group. Role assignments and policies from every parent scope apply to them.

nodes.label: App Service
nodes.detail: Resources in the same RG can be in different regions.

nodes.label: Storage account
nodes.detail: A lock on rg-data-prod would protect this storage account from deletion.

nodes.label: VNet
nodes.detail: Tags placed on the RG are not inherited by this resource unless Azure Policy copies them.

steps.title: The tenant
steps.text: Identity lives in the Entra tenant. Every subscription trusts one tenant for authentication.

steps.title: Management groups
steps.text: Management groups organize subscriptions. Assign Policy and RBAC here to cover many subscriptions — including ones added later.

steps.title: Subscriptions
steps.text: Subscriptions are billing and scale boundaries; each sits in exactly one management group.

steps.title: Resource groups and resources
steps.text: Resource groups hold resources that share a lifecycle. Each resource belongs to exactly one RG.

steps.title: Inheritance path
steps.text: A role or policy assigned at Production MG flows to Subscription A, RG web-prod and the VM. Tags do not inherit by default.

examExpects: Assign policies and roles at the highest scope that matches the requirement to minimize effort — a management group covers all current and future subscriptions under it.
Each subscription and management group has one parent; resources belong to exactly one resource group.
RBAC role assignments, Azure Policy assignments and resource locks inherit downward; tags do not.
Resource group location is metadata only — use Policy to restrict resource locations.

title: Azure RBAC Scope Inheritance
summary: How role assignments at different scopes combine into a user's effective permissions.

nodes.label: Management group
nodes.detail: An assignment here applies to every subscription, resource group and resource below it.

nodes.label: Subscription
nodes.detail: Inherits the Reader assignment from the management group.

nodes.label: Resource group
nodes.detail: Has its own Contributor assignment for Alex, plus inherited Reader for the Ops group.

nodes.label: Virtual machine
nodes.detail: Alex can modify this VM because Contributor at RG-App is inherited by the VM.

nodes.label: Reader
nodes.detail: Role assignment = principal + role definition + scope. Reader can view but not change resources.

nodes.label: Contributor
nodes.detail: Contributor can manage resources but cannot grant access to others.

nodes.label: Ops-Readers
nodes.detail: Assigning roles to groups instead of users minimizes administrative effort.

nodes.label: Alex
nodes.detail: Alex receives Reader through the group and Contributor directly.

nodes.label: Alex's effective access
nodes.detail: Permissions are additive: the union of all assignments that apply. Only deny assignments can subtract.

steps.title: A role assignment has three parts
steps.text: Who (Ops-Readers group) + what (Reader role) + where (MG Corp).

steps.title: Assignments inherit down
steps.text: Reader at the management group flows to the subscription, RG-App and the VM.

steps.title: A second assignment
steps.text: Alex is also directly assigned Contributor at RG-App.

steps.title: Permissions add up
steps.text: Alex can read everything under Corp and modify resources in RG-App — but cannot assign roles, because neither Reader nor Contributor includes role assignment.

examExpects: Read a set of assignments and work out effective access: union of all roles across group memberships and parent scopes.
Pick the narrowest scope and least-privileged built-in role that meets the requirement.
Contributor can't grant access; Owner, User Access Administrator or RBAC Administrator can.
NotActions aren't denies; only deny assignments override grants.

title: Azure Policy Inheritance & Exclusions
summary: A policy assigned at a management group evaluates every child scope, except scopes you exclude.

nodes.label: Allowed locations
nodes.detail: A built-in policy definition with a parameter listing permitted regions (here East US and West US). Effect: Deny.

nodes.label: Management group: Corp
nodes.detail: Assigning at the management group evaluates every subscription under it, including future ones.

nodes.label: Subscription: Prod
nodes.detail: Inherits the assignment automatically — no per-subscription configuration.

nodes.label: Subscription: Dev
nodes.detail: Also inherits the assignment.

nodes.label: RG: app-prod
nodes.detail: Resources here are evaluated against the policy.

nodes.label: RG: research
nodes.detail: An exclusion (notScopes) on the assignment removes this RG from evaluation. Use exemptions for time-bound or documented waivers.

nodes.label: RG: dev-tools
nodes.detail: Evaluated like any other child scope.

nodes.label: VM in East US
nodes.detail: Matches the allowed list, so the deployment succeeds and the resource is compliant.

nodes.label: VM in Japan East
nodes.detail: Because the RG is excluded, the policy doesn't apply and the deployment succeeds.

nodes.label: VM in Japan East
nodes.detail: Deny blocks the create request at Resource Manager — even for an Owner.

steps.title: Assign once, high up
steps.text: The Allowed locations policy is assigned at the Corp management group.

steps.title: Inheritance
steps.text: Every subscription and resource group under Corp is evaluated.

steps.title: Exclusion
steps.text: RG research is excluded on the assignment, so nothing there is evaluated.

steps.title: Deny at request time
steps.text: A VM in a disallowed region is blocked before it's created. Existing resources are only reported as non-compliant — Deny never deletes them.

examExpects: Assign at the management group to cover all subscriptions with the least effort; use exclusions or exemptions for exceptions.
Deny prevents new non-compliant resources; Audit only reports. Existing resources aren't changed by Deny.
Modify/DeployIfNotExists can fix resources; existing ones need a remediation task and a managed identity.
Policy applies regardless of the user's RBAC role.

title: Azure Identity Relationships
summary: How users, guests, groups, administrative units, Entra roles and Azure RBAC relate inside a tenant and its subscriptions.

nodes.label: Member users
nodes.detail: Cloud-only users are created in Entra ID; synchronized users come from on-premises AD via Entra Connect/Cloud Sync.

nodes.label: Guest users
nodes.detail: External identities invited via B2B collaboration; they sign in with their home credentials.

nodes.label: Managed identities
nodes.detail: Identities for apps and Azure resources, with no secrets to manage. Can be assigned RBAC roles.

nodes.label: Security groups
nodes.detail: Groups simplify access: assign roles, apps and licenses to the group. Dynamic membership needs Entra ID P1+.

nodes.label: Administrative unit
nodes.detail: Restricts the scope of Entra roles to its members.

nodes.label: Entra role
nodes.detail: Directory roles manage identities and tenant settings. Scoped to the tenant, an AU or an app.

nodes.label: Subscription
nodes.detail: Subscriptions rely on the tenant for authentication; they can be moved to another tenant (which removes existing RBAC assignments).

nodes.label: RBAC assignment
nodes.detail: Azure RBAC authorizes resource management. Principals can be users, guests, groups, service principals or managed identities.

nodes.label: Azure resources
nodes.detail: Access is evaluated by Azure Resource Manager using RBAC assignments at the resource and its parent scopes.

steps.title: Identities
steps.text: The tenant holds members, guests and workload identities such as managed identities.

steps.title: Groups
steps.text: Put identities in security groups and assign access to the group.

steps.title: Directory administration
steps.text: Entra roles manage the directory. Scope them to administrative units to delegate a subset of users.

steps.title: Resource access
steps.text: Azure RBAC role assignments (to groups or managed identities) authorize work on resources in subscriptions that trust this tenant.

examExpects: Entra roles (directory) and Azure RBAC roles (resources) are separate systems.
Guests can receive RBAC roles and group memberships like members.
Administrative units scope Entra roles, not Azure resource access.
Managed identities are the preferred way to give Azure resources access to other resources.
